title: Zéro French
tagline: A free, project-based curriculum that takes you from zero French to passing the TCF Canada.

paths.title: A1 Basics
paths.description: Start from zero: learn the French alphabet, pronunciation, greetings, basic grammar and everyday vocabulary.

sections.title: Foundations & Pronunciation
sections.description: Master the French alphabet, accents, vowel mechanics, nasal sounds, and core phonetic rules.

lessons.title: The Alphabet, Accents, and Spelling
lessons.description: Learn the 26 French letters, avoid English letter traps (G/J, E/I/U), master the 5 accents, and dictate Canadian postal codes and emails.

lessons.title: Pure Vowels, U vs OU, and Nasal Sounds
lessons.description: Master French monophthongs, the tricky U (/y/) versus OU (/u/) distinction, and the three core nasal vowels (an, on, in).

lessons.title: Silent Letters, Elision, and Liaisons
lessons.description: Learn the CaReFuL final consonant rule, elision with apostrophes, mandatory vs forbidden liaisons, and phonetic shifts (s/x to /z/, d to /t/).

lessons.title: Numbers, Time, and the Calendar
lessons.description: Master cardinal numbers 0 to 100+, the vigesimal system (70–99), telling time in 12h/24h systems, days, months, and Canadian date conventions.

lessons.title: Project: Pronunciation Benchmark
lessons.description: Record an audio benchmark testing vowel contrasts (U vs OU), nasal vowels, silent letters, liaisons, and numbers.

sections.title: Greetings & Introductions
sections.description: Say hello, introduce yourself, and understand basic polite phrases in French.

lessons.title: Greetings and Politeness
lessons.description: Learn to greet people formally and informally, say goodbye, and use basic polite expressions.

lessons.title: Personal Identity and Essential Verbs
lessons.description: State your name, nationality, age, and profession using the essential verbs être and avoir.

lessons.title: Family and Relationships
lessons.description: Describe immediate family members, marital status, and express relationships using possessive adjectives.

lessons.title: Everyday Objects and Grammatical Gender
lessons.description: Name common home and workplace objects, master definite and indefinite articles (le, la, un, une), and describe items with basic colors.

lessons.title: Project: Introduce Yourself
lessons.description: Record a short self-introduction in French using the greetings and polite phrases you have learned.

sections.title: Daily Routine & Places
sections.description: Conjugate regular verbs, talk about your daily schedule, and navigate buildings and town landmarks.

lessons.title: Regular -er Verbs and Daily Actions
lessons.description: Conjugate present tense regular -er verbs for routine morning and evening activities, work, and leisure.

lessons.title: The Essential Irregular Triad: Aller, Faire, Venir
lessons.description: Master the high-frequency verbs aller, faire, and venir to describe movement, activities, weather expressions, and immediate future/past actions.

lessons.title: Asking Questions and Essential Interrogatives
lessons.description: Formulate questions in French using intonation, est-ce que, and the core interrogatives (qui, que, où, quand, comment, pourquoi, combien).

lessons.title: Places in Town and Navigation Prepositions
lessons.description: Identify municipal landmarks, master spatial prepositions with contractions (à côté de, en face de, près de), and give directions.

lessons.title: Project: Daily Routine & Neighborhood
lessons.description: Write a 60–120 word email to a friend describing your daily schedule, living area, and extending an invitation under timed TCF-SO conditions.

sections.title: Food, Shopping & Basic Needs
sections.description: Navigate grocery stores and markets, master partitive articles, order at cafés, describe clothing, and discuss weather.

lessons.title: Food, Groceries, and Partitive Articles
lessons.description: Master essential food vocabulary, supermarket departments, and partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) versus definite articles.

lessons.title: Ordering at a Café and Polite Transactions
lessons.description: Order coffee, pastries, and lunch at counters, master the polite conditional je voudrais, ask prices, and settle bills in France and Canada.

lessons.title: Clothing, Sizes, and Adjective Agreements
lessons.description: Name everyday garments and winter outerwear, master gender and number adjective agreements, color rules, and shopping mechanics.

lessons.title: Weather, Seasons, and Temperatures
lessons.description: Describe atmospheric conditions using impersonal verbs (il fait, il pleut, il neige), state temperatures, and master season prepositions.

lessons.title: Project: A1 Capstone Challenge
lessons.description: Demonstrate complete A1 mastery with a 3-minute oral interaction inquiry and a timed 60–80 word practical message under TCF Canada conditions.

paths.title: A2 Survival French
paths.description: Handle day-to-day interactions: narrate past events, ask detailed questions, navigate housing and transport, and communicate with public services.

sections.title: Past Narratives & Daily Life
sections.description: Master compound past tenses (passé composé with avoir and être), sequence events chronologically, and decode everyday announcements.

lessons.title: Passé Composé with Avoir and Past Participles
lessons.description: Form the passé composé with auxiliary avoir, master regular and irregular past participles, and place negations and adverbs correctly.

lessons.title: Passé Composé with Être and Past Agreement
lessons.description: Master movement verbs (DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP), reflexive verbs in the past, and mandatory past participle gender and number agreement.

lessons.title: Narrative Chronology and Discourse Connectors
lessons.description: Structure past anecdotes step-by-step using narrative markers (d'abord, ensuite, puis, soudain, tout à coup, enfin, finalement).

lessons.title: TCF Listening: Short Announcements and Messages
lessons.description: Decode public address announcements, transit advisories, commercial messages, and voicemails under TCF single-play conditions.

lessons.title: Project: Past Vacation Recount
lessons.description: Compose an 80–120 word written recount and deliver a 2-minute unscripted oral narrative of a past vacation or journey under TCF exam conditions.

sections.title: Housing & Transit
sections.description: Navigate rental listings, understand real estate abbreviations, lease agreements, and communicate about housing.

lessons.title: Apartment Features, Real Estate Ads, and Rental Terms
lessons.description: Read classified real estate ads, decode abbreviations (rdc, asc., sdb, cc), and master European versus Canadian room sizing systems (1½ to 5½).

lessons.title: Imparfait: Descriptions, States, and Past Habits
lessons.description: Form the imperfect tense using the regular nous stem, master the irregular être stem (ét-), and describe past settings, weather, and routines.

lessons.title: Direct and Indirect Object Pronouns: Le, La, Les, Lui, Leur
lessons.description: Replace repeated nouns using direct pronouns (le, la, les) and indirect pronouns (lui, leur) and master pronoun placement before verbs and auxiliaries.

lessons.title: Formal Questioning Techniques: Inversion, Est-ce que, and Indirect Openers
lessons.description: Master subject-verb inversion, euphonic -t- insertion, complex noun inversion, and polite indirect question openers for TCF Speaking Task 2.

lessons.title: Project: Apartment Inquiry Roleplay
lessons.description: Lead a 3.5-minute unscripted telephone inquiry roleplay asking 8–10 formal questions to a landlord under TCF Speaking Task 2 conditions.

sections.title: Work & Daily Life
sections.description: Describe professional duties, work schedules, job titles, and contrast compound past and imperfect tenses in workplace narratives.

lessons.title: Professions, Job Titles, and Workplace Tasks
lessons.description: Master Canadian gender-inclusive job titles, action verbs for workplace responsibilities (gérer, rédiger, animer), schedules, and telework.

lessons.title: Passé Composé vs Imparfait: Backdrop vs Event
lessons.description: Master the defining contrast of French past narration: continuous descriptive backdrops (imparfait) versus completed punctual events (passé composé).

lessons.title: Futur Proche and Futur Simple: Plans and Projections
lessons.description: Express immediate plans with futur proche (aller + infinitive) and long-term career aspirations with futur simple, mastering irregular stems.

lessons.title: Comparisons and Superlatives: Evaluating Options
lessons.description: Compare qualities, quantities, and actions using plus, moins, aussi, and autant de, mastering the irregular distinction between meilleur and mieux.

lessons.title: Project: Career Profile and Professional Goals
lessons.description: Compose a 100–120 word professional cover note and deliver a 2-minute unscripted oral career presentation under TCF Canada exam conditions.

sections.title: Health & Public Services
sections.description: Communicate medical symptoms, seek health advice, use pronouns y and en, and interact politely with public administrations and services.

lessons.title: Medical Symptoms, Doctor Visits, and Imperative Advice
lessons.description: Express physical pain with avoir mal à, describe sensations and illnesses, navigate clinics and pharmacies, and give medical guidance.

lessons.title: Adverbial and Prepositional Pronouns: Y and En
lessons.description: Master place and preposition replacement with y (locations and à + thing) and partitive/quantity replacement with en (de + thing).

lessons.title: Administrative Interactions and Counter Etiquette
lessons.description: Master formal counter etiquette (vouvoiement), polite conditional requests, administrative documents, and postal/banking interactions.

lessons.title: TCF Reading: Public Signage, Notices, and Classified Ads
lessons.description: Fast scanning and skimming of street signs, safety warnings, store hours, rental ads, and municipal directives for items 1–12.

lessons.title: Project: A2 Milestone Mock Exam
lessons.description: Demonstrate complete A2 survival French with a 4-part milestone mock exam evaluating listening, reading, writing, and speaking under TCF conditions.

paths.title: B1 Independent French
paths.description: Achieve functional autonomy: express nuanced opinions, formulate hypotheses, negotiate professionally, and master the subjunctive mood.

sections.title: Politeness & Hypotheses
sections.description: Master polite conditional requests, si-clause hypothetical structures, workplace negotiations, and formal dispute resolution.

lessons.title: The Present Conditional: Politeness, Advice, and Wishes
lessons.description: Form the conditionnel présent with future stems and imperfect endings, soften requests diplomatically, and offer professional advice.

lessons.title: Hypothetical Sentences: Si Clauses Structures 1 and 2
lessons.description: Master real future conditions (si + présent → futur) and potential present conditions (si + imparfait → conditionnel).

lessons.title: Workplace Negotiations, Disputes, and Diplomatic Compromises
lessons.description: Express professional dissatisfaction diplomatically, negotiate schedule adjustments and deadlines, and draft formal dispute emails.

lessons.title: TCF Speaking Task 2: Advanced Interaction and Negotiation
lessons.description: Lead 3.5-minute unscripted roleplays, challenge examiner objections, formulate counter-proposals, and negotiate agreements.

lessons.title: Project: Writing Task 2 Formal Letter Simulation
lessons.description: Compose a 120–150 word formal diplomatic dispute and negotiation email to a supervisor under official TCF Canada conditions.

sections.title: Opinions & Social Debates
sections.description: Articulate nuanced personal viewpoints, master the subjunctive mood and its triggers, structure concessions, and engage in societal debates.

lessons.title: Expressing Viewpoints, Nuance, and Degrees of Certainty
lessons.description: Master sophisticated opinion markers (selon moi, à mon sens, il me paraît évident que), calibrate certainty, and formulate concessions.

lessons.title: The Present Subjunctive: Formation and Essential Triggers
lessons.description: Form the subjonctif présent with regular and irregular stems, and master the four trigger categories: obligation, will, emotion, and doubt.

lessons.title: Indicative vs Subjunctive: Deciding Moods and Avoiding Traps
lessons.description: Master the decisive boundary between fact (indicatif) and perception (subjonctif), opinion verb polarity, and avoid false triggers like espérer.

lessons.title: Structuring Arguments, Concession, and Counter-Arguments
lessons.description: Master concession markers (certes... mais, bien que, toutefois, en revanche), construct balanced dialectical syntheses, and debate social issues.

lessons.title: Project: Speaking Task 3 Monologue Simulator
lessons.description: Deliver an unscripted 4.5-minute dialectical debate monologue on telework and modern labor practices under official TCF Canada conditions.

sections.title: Media & Society
sections.description: Decode Francophone journalism, follow rapid news radio bulletins, construct complex relative clauses, and report statements accurately.

lessons.title: Reading Francophone Press: Structure, Headlines, and Tone
lessons.description: Navigate Francophone newspapers (Le Monde, Le Devoir, La Presse), analyze inverted pyramid structures, and decode journalistic headlines.

lessons.title: Radio Bulletins: Following RFI and Radio-Canada Cadences
lessons.description: Train ears to professional radio cadences, decode rapid audio dispatches, and extract essential news facts under single-play conditions.

lessons.title: Complex Sentence Building: Relative Pronouns Qui, Que, Où, and Dont
lessons.description: Master simple relative pronouns (qui, que, où, dont) and compound relatives (ce qui, ce que, ce dont) to build sophisticated sentences without repetition.

lessons.title: Reported Speech in the Present: Relaying News, Statements, and Interviews
lessons.description: Master indirect discourse with present-tense reporting verbs, transform questions and commands, adjust pronouns, and use nuanced attribution verbs.

lessons.title: Project: Current Event Digest and Oral News Briefing
lessons.description: Synthesize conflicting journalistic sources into a 120-word written digest and deliver a 3-minute unscripted radio news dispatch under TCF Canada conditions.

sections.title: Canadian Realities
sections.description: Understand Canadian and Quebec societal frameworks, immigration systems, regional integration, and distinct sociolinguistic conventions.

lessons.title: Canadian Immigration and Integration: Systems, Regions, and Society
lessons.description: Navigate Canadian and Quebec immigration structures (IRCC, MIFI, Express Entry, CSQ), analyze regionalization policies, and debate integration models.

lessons.title: Quebec French Lexicon and Phonology: Everyday Terms, Affrication, and Registers
lessons.description: Master distinct Canadian French vocabulary (courriel, fin de semaine, char), decode affrication ([ts], [dz]) and vowel shifts, and navigate formal vs colloquial registers.

lessons.title: B1 Discourse Connectors and Logical Articulators: Building Textual Cohesion
lessons.description: Master structured discourse markers (en premier lieu, d'une part, néanmoins, par conséquent, ainsi), avoid false traps, and construct coherent paragraphs.

lessons.title: TCF Canada B1 Listening and Reading Tactics: Mastering Items 1 to 25
lessons.description: Master single-play listening protocols, reading pacing grids, and binary elimination strategies to achieve near-perfect accuracy on items 1 to 25.

lessons.title: Project: B1 Milestone Mock Examination
lessons.description: Complete a full 4-part B1 milestone mock exam evaluating listening (25 items), reading (25 items), writing (Tasks 1 & 2), and speaking (Tasks 1, 2, 3) under official TCF Canada conditions.

paths.title: B2 Advanced French
paths.description: Master nuanced argumentation, dialectical synthesis, complex radio debates, administrative nominalization, and advanced exam tactics for NCLC 7+.

sections.title: Argumentation Mastery
sections.description: Structure persuasive dialectical essays, elevate stylistic register through nominalization, and master advanced rhetorical strategies.

lessons.title: Structuring Persuasive Essays at B2: Problem Statements, Dialectical Plans, and Formal Synthesis
lessons.description: Master tripartite dialectical plans (thèse, antithèse, synthèse), formulate precise problem statements, and execute concessive counterargument refutations.

lessons.title: Nominalization and Register Elevation: Administrative and Academic Style
lessons.description: Elevate conversational verbal structures into formal nominal phrases, master suffixation paradigms, and achieve high informational density.

lessons.title: Advanced Logical Articulators: Proportionality, Hypothesis, and Concession
lessons.description: Master sophisticated B2 connectors (d'autant plus que, nonobstant, quand bien même, pourvu que, quitte à), and govern subjunctive and conditional moods.

lessons.title: Nuance and Modalization: Calibrating Certainty, Probability, and Rhetorical Distance
lessons.description: Master epistemic verbs (devoir, sembler), the journalistic conditional, modal adverbs, and impersonal frames to defend nuanced B2 arguments.

lessons.title: Project: Writing Task 3 Foundations
lessons.description: Synthesize two conflicting journalistic sources and defend a nuanced B2 dialectical position in a timed 120–180 word essay under official TCF Canada conditions.

sections.title: Complex Audio & Voices
sections.description: Decode rapid spontaneous French, overcome acoustic interference and overlapping turn-taking, and master North American Francophone accents.

lessons.title: Decoding Rapid Spontaneous Speech: Phonetic Reductions, Ambient Noise, and Turn-Taking
lessons.description: Master conversational reductions (ch'sais pas, y a, pronoun drops), track rhythmic tonic accents through ambient noise, and navigate rapid debate turn-taking.

lessons.title: Radio-Canada Podcasts Analysis: Macro-Listening and Institutional Registers
lessons.description: Deconstruct long-format public affairs podcasts from Radio-Canada, decode Canadian civic vocabulary, and extract implicit editorial stances under single-play exam conditions.

lessons.title: Canadian Accents and Idioms: Diphthongization, Contractions, and Authentic Colloquialisms
lessons.description: Master the phonetics of spoken Canadian French (affrication, laxing, diphthongs), decipher colloquial discourse markers, and decode high-frequency idioms.

lessons.title: TCF Listening Advanced Drills: Dissecting Items 26–39 and Distractor Traps
lessons.description: Master the 10-second prediction protocol, identify the 4 universal distractor mechanisms (lexical recycling, polarity inversion, over-generalization, chronological shift), and tackle upper-tier audio under single-play conditions.

lessons.title: Project: TCF Listening Sprint
lessons.description: Complete a full timed 14-item listening sprint targeting items 26–39, diagnose error patterns with the distractor taxonomy, and calibrate raw scores to NCLC 7 thresholds.

sections.title: Editorial Reading & Text Analysis
sections.description: Deconstruct complex journalistic and academic prose, decode subtle rhetorical stance, and master rapid reading tactics for items 26–39.

lessons.title: Analyzing Academic and Journalistic Texts: Macro-Reading, Text Architecture, and Informational Density
lessons.description: Deconstruct the 5-part architecture of French essays and white papers, unpack dense nominalization chains, and master the 3-pass macro-reading strategy.

lessons.title: Detecting Bias, Irony, and Implied Meaning: Rhetorical Stance and Subtext
lessons.description: Decode authorial stance through scare quotes, the journalistic conditional, value-laden lexicon, antiphrasis, and litotes under TCF exam conditions.

lessons.title: TCF Reading Advanced Drills: Pacing Tactics and the 3-Tier Blueprint
lessons.description: Master the 3-tier pacing strategy, bank 20+ minutes for items 28–39, navigate the 4 upper-tier question categories, and apply the 5-step surgical reading protocol.

lessons.title: Fast Elimination and Keyword Traps: Neutralizing Distractors and False Friends
lessons.description: Dismantle absolute wording traps, false friends, lexical echoes, and plausible extrapolations using the fast elimination algorithm and the slightly softer paraphrase rule.

lessons.title: Project: TCF Reading Marathon
lessons.description: Complete a full timed 15-item reading sprint (items 25–39), diagnose error patterns with the distractor taxonomy, and calibrate raw scores to NCLC 7 thresholds.

sections.title: High-Stakes Production
sections.description: Master timed computer-based essay writing and high-pressure speaking tasks under official TCF Canada conditions.

lessons.title: Writing Task 1 Perfection: Precise Register, 12-Minute Budget, and Zero Word-Count Penalty
lessons.description: Master the 60–120 word boundary, maintain rigorous register consistency, and satisfy all prompt requirements in under 12 minutes.

lessons.title: Writing Task 2 Perfection: Balancing Personal Recount and Critical Civic Opinion
lessons.description: Master the 120–150 word boundary, execute the 50/50 bipartite architecture, and elevate narrative recounts into mature B2 civic argumentation in under 18 minutes.

lessons.title: Writing Task 3 Perfection: Radical Paraphrase, Document Synthesis, and Dialectical Stance
lessons.description: Synthesize two opposing source texts without verbatim copying, target the 145–165 word sweet spot, and defend a nuanced dialectical thesis under strict 28-minute exam timing.

lessons.title: Speaking Task 2 & 3 B2 Tactics: Roleplay Leadership and the 4.5-Minute Monologue
lessons.description: Lead the examiner in Task 2 through structured inquiries and objection negotiation, and sustain an articulate 4.5-minute unscripted monologue in Task 3.

lessons.title: Project: B2 Milestone Mock Exam
lessons.description: Complete a full 4-skill timed milestone mock exam (CO 35m, CE 60m, EE 60m, EO 12m) to evaluate and certify the NCLC 7 benchmark.

paths.title: TCF Canada Exam Prep
paths.description: Master test psychology, rapid predictive listening, high-speed typing without spellcheck, unscripted speaking under pressure, and full-dress rehearsal mocks.

sections.title: Exam Mechanics & Distractor Dissection
sections.description: Deconstruct the psychometric architecture of the TCF Canada, master predictive listening scanning, and defeat deceptive distractor traps.

lessons.title: Listening Prediction and Choice Scanning: Weaponizing the 10-Second Preview Window
lessons.description: Master the 10-second eye sweep protocol, map semantic fault lines, prime lexical fields, and overcome the choice freezing trap.

lessons.title: Distractor Dissection: Catching False Friends, Reversed Polarity, and Chronological Misdirection
lessons.description: Neutralize restrictive negations (ne... que, guère), false friends (éventuellement, ignorer), and chronological misdirection using the fast elimination protocol.

lessons.title: Reading Pacing Blueprint: Strict 15 / 15 / 30 Time Allocation
lessons.description: Master the 15/15/30 time budget, monitor four clock checkpoints on the computer screen, and execute emergency triage under time pressure.

lessons.title: The Five-Second Drop Rule: Emotional Resilience and Halting Domino Collapses
lessons.description: Master the four-step five-second drop protocol, eliminate the sunk cost fallacy, and deploy somatic grounding to recover from testing blackouts.

lessons.title: Project: Back-to-Back Timed MCQ Sprint
lessons.description: Execute a full 95-minute continuous sitting combining the 35-minute Listening test and 60-minute Reading test under strict TCF-SO computer rules.

sections.title: Writing Speed & Precision Under Pressure
sections.description: Master typing French accents without autocorrect, calibrate exact word-count boundaries, and drill timed execution across all three writing tasks.

lessons.title: Typing French Under Exam Conditions: Keyboard Muscle Memory and Zero-Autocorrect Mastery
lessons.description: Configure physical keyboards, master dead-key combinations on US-International and Canadian Multilingual, eliminate accent-related grammatical slips, and benchmark typing speed.

lessons.title: Writing Task 1 Speed Drill: 80 Words in 12 Minutes with 3 Minutes of Proofreading
lessons.description: Master rapid message drafting under strict 15-minute exam limits: modular opening formulas, precise informational delivery, and systematic proofreading.

lessons.title: Writing Task 2 Speed Drill: 135 Words in 16 Minutes with 4 Minutes of Proofreading
lessons.description: Execute the 50/50 narrative recount and civic opinion letter in 20 minutes flat, calibrating word counts and deploying transitional articulators under time pressure.

lessons.title: Writing Task 3 Speed Drill: 150 Words Synthesis and Stance in 20 Minutes with 5 Minutes Proofreading
lessons.description: Master the 25-minute synthesis and opinion challenge: rapid document comparison, zero-copying paraphrasing strategies, and structured dialectical argumentation.

lessons.title: Project: Full 60-Minute Timed Writing Simulation
lessons.description: Complete the entire 3-task TCF Canada Expression écrite sitting in 60 minutes sharp without autocorrect or word-counter plugins, evaluated against official FEI criteria.

sections.title: Speaking Under Pressure & Spontaneous Interaction
sections.description: Master unscripted self-introductions, rapid 2-minute scrap paper preparation, 4.5-minute monologue architecture, and psychological recovery from oral freezes.

lessons.title: Task 1 Modular Intro Framework: The 2-Minute Unscripted Self-Presentation
lessons.description: Master the four-module self-intro architecture, eliminate monosyllabic stalls, deploy high-register B2 biographical syntax, and handle spontaneous examiner interruptions.

lessons.title: Task 2 Two-Minute Prep Template: Shorthand Grids and Interactive Roleplay Leadership
lessons.description: Overcome full-sentence paralysis with the 6-W + 4-T shorthand grid, vary question syntax across four grammatical registers, and negotiate examiner roadblocks during the 3.5-minute roleplay.

lessons.title: Task 3 Sustaining the Monologue: The Rule of Three and 4.5-Minute Endurance
lessons.description: Master the 5-phase monologue roadmap, apply the Rule of Three to decompose societal dilemmas, anchor claims in Canadian reality, and sustain unscripted speech for 4.5 minutes.

lessons.title: Overcoming Hesitations & Recovery: High-Register Fillers and Surgical Self-Repair
lessons.description: Replace vocalized pauses with authoritative rhetorical fillers, climb the 3-rung circumlocution ladder during lexical blackouts, and execute surgical grammatical self-repairs.

lessons.title: Project: Full 12-Minute Timed Speaking Simulation
lessons.description: Execute the entire three-task TCF Canada Expression orale test in 12 continuous minutes with recorded evidence, evaluated against official FEI criteria.

sections.title: Full Rehearsals & Test-Day Logistics
sections.description: Execute full-dress 3-hour examination rehearsals under official test-center conditions, diagnose performance vulnerabilities, and manage test-day logistics.

lessons.title: Rehearsal Exam 1 Protocol: The Full-Dress 3-Hour Simulation Setup
lessons.description: Configure the 4-stage mock sitting environment, manage cognitive stamina during the 10-minute intermission, and execute a post-mock diagnostic error autopsy.

lessons.title: Diagnostic Recovery Blueprint: Error Triage and the 7-Day Remedial Sprint
lessons.description: Triage Mock Sitting #1 across the 4 failure modes, deploy micro-drills to reclaim lost points, and execute a structured 7-day remedial sprint.

lessons.title: Rehearsal Exam 2 Protocol: Testing Under Adversity and Safety Margin Calculation
lessons.description: Execute Mock Sitting #2 under deliberate ambient interference, compute comparative performance deltas, and calculate your NCLC Safety Margin Index.

lessons.title: Test-Day Logistics & Performance Psychology: Arrival, Calibrations, and Somatic Regulation
lessons.description: Master the T-24 documentation audit, terminal calibration checks, biological glycemic management, and somatic nervous-system regulation.

lessons.title: Project: Final Readiness Audit & NCLC Score Verification
lessons.description: Execute a comprehensive evidence portfolio audit across all 4 skills, calculate your Safety Margin Index, and apply the 7-criteria Go/No-Go decision gate.

paths.title: B2+ Safety Margin (C1 Foundations)
paths.description: Push comfortably into C1 territory (NCLC 8–9) to make NCLC 7 immune to bad test-day conditions: literary past tense recognition, counterfactual conditionnel passé, advanced concordance, and unscripted debate defense.

sections.title: Advanced Syntax & Literary Grammar Recognition
sections.description: Master passive recognition of literary past tenses, counterfactual conditional hypotheses, past subjunctive concordances, and implicit cultural idioms.

lessons.title: Passé Simple Recognition: Decoding Literary and Journalistic Past Tenses in High-Difficulty Texts
lessons.description: Recognize the 4 vowel-ending paradigms of the passé simple in Reading items 28–39, decouple tricky homophones, and trace chronological narratives.

lessons.title: Conditionnel Passé & Unfulfilled Hypotheses: Regrets, Reproaches, and Precautionary Tone
lessons.description: Conjugate the conditionnel passé, master the third hypothetical conditional (Si + plus-que-parfait), formulate diplomatic policy critiques, and decode journalistic speculation.

lessons.title: Subjonctif Passé & Concordance des Temps: Expressing Anteriority in Evaluation
lessons.description: Form the subjonctif passé, master tense agreement rules after evaluative matrices, and elevate writing conclusions.

lessons.title: Cultural Metaphors and Idioms in Canadian Political and Civic Discourse
lessons.description: Decode implicit idioms and figurative expressions in Canadian public debate, editorials, and high-difficulty reading texts.

lessons.title: Project: C1 200-Word Deep-Dive Argumentative Essay
lessons.description: Compose an unassisted 200-word argumentative essay on technological governance integrating past subjunctive, counterfactuals, and civic idioms.

sections.title: Spontaneous Debate & Rhetorical Fluency
sections.description: Defend complex and counter-intuitive prompts with zero preparation, master high-register spoken connectors, and refine French rhythmic cadence.

lessons.title: Counter-Intuitive Prompt Defense: Unscripted Stance Articulation Under Adversarial Pressure
lessons.description: Dissect provocative speaking prompts, apply the 3-step reframing protocol, deploy diplomatic concession formulas, and sustain a 4.5-minute monologue.

lessons.title: Sophisticated Rhetorical Connectors: Elevating Discursive Cohesion to C1 Mastery
lessons.description: Master advanced discursive tools (non seulement... mais bien plus, qui plus est, d'autant que, loin s'en faut, quand bien même) and their mood constraints.

lessons.title: Pronunciation, Intonation, and Cadence: Eliminating English Stress Patterns and Mastering French Rhythmic Groups
lessons.description: Transition from stress-timed English prosody to French syllable-timed rhythm, master rhythmic groups, tonic prolongation, and emphatic accentuation.

lessons.title: Project: C1 5-Minute Unscripted Spoken Defense Challenge
lessons.description: Deliver an unscripted 2-minute monologue on civil liberties and biometric surveillance, followed by a 3-minute defense responding to hostile examiner cross-examination.

lessons.title: Project: Full-Dress Safety Margin Final Mock Examination (NCLC 8–9 Calibration)
lessons.description: Execute a complete 4-skill mock simulation (CO 35m, CE 60m, EE 60m, EO 12m) calibrated to C1/NCLC 8–9 thresholds to ensure an unshakeable B2 immigration safety buffer.
